results.reason: The response states the First Supplement window closed on September 28. It says that under §5.7(c), Ferrovane is cured for Article IX indemnity and for the §7.2(a) bring-down condition. It also notes the walk right is effectively lost.

The response explains that the Escrow §1.1/§4.3 'Losses' definition is out-of-pocket only and excludes diminution in value and attorneys' fees. It cites SPA §11.11 giving the Escrow Agreement control over disbursement mechanics, and explains this limits what Buyer can recover from the escrow.

The response identifies MSA §14.2 (more than 50% voting equity deemed an assignment requiring prior written consent). It notes the consent is missing from Annex 7.2(d), §5.3 and §7.2(d), and that §4.4 is inaccurate. It explains the termination and List Price repricing risk after closing, plus the weak walk right.
The response states the First Supplement window closed September 28, counting from September 14 in Business Days.
The response states the escrow cap of $4.85M is effectively the whole fund, which identifies the escrow amount.
The memo is addressed to the Partner. Each issue gives a Where/section location, a Why it matters discussion and a Recommended fix.
Section 4 ('Items I could not resolve from the documents') and Section 5 ('Client input needed') cover this, along with open items under each issue.
The response states the First Supplement window has closed and Ferrovane is cured. It does not claim a live termination right.
The response states that Annex 7.2(d) lists only the Lender payoff and lien release, and recommends adding the Tavinor consent.
